items.finding: The source notes that OH band temperature sensitivity is a severe drawback for aqueous NIR and MIR measurements, making tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: For MIR ATR (O1), this suggests temperature control of the sample is important; a temperature sensor could help monitor or control the dissolution medium.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns NIR/MIR aqueous measurements and tempered sample holders, not an in-line temperature sensor in a dissolution vessel.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E01 ¶12

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into one new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: Supports O3's low-level fusion baseline; test that Raman and MIR variables are placed in a common matrix and aligned to a common time step.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general PAT review, not a dissolution study or a specific probe setup; it does not detail time alignment or small-volume sampling.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The source reports that in some cases instrument complementarity alone did not improve prediction of several CQAs, citing a Raman and FT-IR food study.
items.how_it_applies: For O3, this is a reason to verify on held-out runs that the fused model beats the best single method before keeping the extra instrument.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study is food analytical, not dissolution; it used Raman and FT-IR, not necessarily Raman and MIR ATR, and was laboratory-based.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E02 ¶36
